WF-001.head: Write burst of 4 words to the message window of context 1 (64-bit bus)
WF-001.note: Cycle 2: AW handshake. Cycles 3 to 6: four W beats, wstrb all ones, wlast on the fourth. Level counts the words in the input FIFO of context 1.

WF-002.head: Write burst with a partial write strobe is rejected with SLVERR
WF-002.note: Beat 2 has wstrb 0F: both beats are accepted and dropped, bresp is SLVERR, error kind 4 is recorded and the AXI error event is raised.

WF-003.head: Input FIFO full: o_axi_wready low until the sequencer pops a word
WF-003.note: Example FIFO of 3 words. The FIFO is full in cycles 5 to 7 so wready is low and W3 is held; the pop in cycle 7 frees a place and W3 is accepted in cycle 8. No word is dropped.

WF-004.head: Final command, padding and digest ready of a short SHA-256 message
WF-004.note: Cycles 4 to 8 stand for the 66 cycles of one SHA-256 block at UNR 1 (not to scale). The short message fits in one padded block.

WF-005.head: Read burst of the 4-word digest from the digest window of context 1
WF-005.note: The read data are the 4 digest words in standard byte order; the output FIFO level falls with each beat and the context becomes FREE after the last word.

WF-006.head: Read of an empty digest window returns zero and raises the underflow event
WF-006.note: The read completes with OKAY and data 0; error kind 2 is recorded and software learns of it from the underflow event.

WF-007.head: APB write of the init command, then a non-secure write rejected with PSLVERR
WF-007.note: First write (PPROT[1] = 0): accepted, o_sha_cmd_init is raised and cleared by hardware. Second write (PPROT[1] = 1) with i_protect_en and i_slverr_en = 1: PSLVERR, no change. Delays follow the clock ratio (11.4).

WF-008.head: Two contexts interleaved on one core: state read and written around each block
WF-008.note: The core runs a block of context 0, then of context 1, then of context 0 again. The context memory is read before and written after each block. ctxsel changes while the core is busy without disturbing it.

WF-009.head: SHAKE128 output of more than one block: the next block is squeezed when the FIFO has room
WF-009.note: Example numbers: FIFO of 32 words, a block of 21 words. Reads (each pulse stands for a burst of 5 words, not to scale) lower the level; at level 11 the next squeeze starts and the level returns to 32.

WF-010.head: External DMA input channel: 4-phase request and acknowledge, then the burst is written
WF-010.note: req rises, ack rises, req falls, ack falls. The DMA controller then writes the burst of sha_dmac.burst words to the message window as ordinary AXI4 writes.

WF-011.head: External DMA output channel: timeout pads a short digest burst with zeros
WF-011.note: The digest has 3 words, the burst is 4. The timer reaches sha_dmac.tmo = 3, the request is raised, the 4th word is zero padding and sha_dvld.words reports 3.

WF-012.head: Duplicate-core mismatch: gate, lock and alarm responses
WF-012.note: A fault makes core A differ from its duplicate B. The mismatch is registered in cycle 3; the responses (gate, lock, alarm) are active in cycle 4 and the lock stays until the soft reset command.

WF-013.head: Masked core takes seed words from the entropy port
WF-013.note: o_ent_req is held until i_ent_valid; words 3 to 8 are not shown. After the eighth word the PRNG is seeded and the status bit is set.

WF-014.head: Abort of a context with clearing, then the soft reset command
WF-014.note: Abort: the context returns to FREE, its FIFO is emptied and, with sha_sec.zero = 1, the core registers are zeroed within 3 cycles. The soft reset command then clears all contexts.

WF-015.head: Reset assertion and synchronized release in the core and APB domains
WF-015.note: Assertion is asynchronous and immediate; release is synchronized to the clock of the domain. During reset the outputs are 0.

WF-016.head: APB write with asynchronous clocks (ratio 1:4): PREADY waits for the core domain
WF-016.note: i_clk_apb is drawn with a period of 4 cells and i_clk_core with 1 cell. The request crosses to the core domain, the register changes there and PREADY returns after the response crosses back; software waits for PREADY.

WF-017.head: Final command while the core is busy and the input FIFO still holds words
WF-017.note: The command is accepted in cycle 2 and the context becomes FINALIZING at once; the remaining 24 words wait until the core is free in cycle 8, then the padded block starts.

WF-018.head: Message whose last block leaves no room for the length: two final blocks
WF-018.note: sha_len.tail leaves 60 bytes of 64 used. The first final block holds the data and the 0x80 byte; the second holds zeros and the 64-bit length (REQ-FUNC-004).

WF-019.head: Changing the selected context while the core is busy
WF-019.note: Software selects context 1 in cycle 4; the status and level registers then show context 1 (one cycle later) while the core goes on with the block of context 0.
